mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above its 5-year average, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals an active monetary tightening cycle that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profit margins, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) below their 3-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand contraction that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in >60% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS are both below 3mo_MA, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in >60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average signals a manufacturing sector contraction that reduces corporate output and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in >60% of instances when INDPRO < 6mo_MA, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.0% signals strong economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in >60% of instances when GDPC1 q/q growth > 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a policy response to labor market weakness, which typically leads to temporary market volatility and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > prior month and FEDFUNDS < prior month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in >60% of instances when UNRATE rises and FEDFUNDS falls, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer confidence and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in >60% of instances when UNRATE increases by >0.2pp, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
